title: 2025 AMC 10A Problem 23
statement: Triangle \(\triangle ABC\) has side lengths \(AB = 80,\) \(BC = 45,\) and \(AC = 75.\) The bisector of \(\angle B\) and the altitude to side \(AB\) intersect at point \(P.\) What is \(BP?\)

solutions.text: Let the bisector of \(\angle B\) hit \(AC\) at \(D.\) By the Angle Bisector Theorem, \(\frac{AD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{80}{45},\) and since \(AC = 75,\) we get \(AD = 48\) and \(CD = 27.\) Triangles \(BCD\) and \(ACB\) share \(\angle C,\) with adjacent sides in the common ratio \(\tfrac{45}{75}=\tfrac{27}{45}=\tfrac35,\) so they are similar by SAS. Hence \(BD=\tfrac35\cdot80=48=AD,\) making \(\triangle ADB\) isosceles. Put \(\angle DAB=\angle DBA=\theta.\) Because the altitude through \(C\) is perpendicular to \(AB,\) both \(\angle DPC\) and \(\angle DCP\) equal \(90^\circ-\theta.\) Thus \(\triangle CDP\) is isosceles, so \(PD=CD=27.\) Since \(P\) lies on \(BD,\) we get \(BP=BD-PD\) \(=48-27=21.\) Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let the bisector of \(\angle B\) meet \(AC\) at \(D;\) the Angle Bisector Theorem gives \(AD = 48\) and \(CD = 27\)
Show \(BD = 48,\) so \(\triangle ADB\) is isosceles; then angle-chase to find \(\triangle CDP\) isosceles with \(PD = CD\)
